blocks.text: Some major characteristics of computer are:

items: Speed: The data processing speed of the computer is very fast. It can perform millions or billions of calculations in a second. Such speeds are beyond the capability of the human brain.

Accuracy: The accuracy of a computer is about 100%. It produces accurate output if the inputs provided to the computer are accurate and the incorrect input will result in incorrect output. This term is known as GIGO (Garbage In Garbage Out).
Automation: A computer is an automatic machine. It is capable of functioning automatically after the essential data and instructions are provided by the user.
Diligence: It is a diligent machine, which can perform repetitive tasks without being bored and never gets tired. It can work for several hours or days with the same speed and accuracy.

Versatility: A computer is a versatile machine, which means able to do many different things. It can be used in different areas for different tasks using the different programs. It can perform simple mathematical calculations to highly complex and logical manipulations.

blocks.text: Capabilities

The following are the capabilities of computer: The computer is capable of performing the task automatically and producing 100% It is capable of performing different tasks in different areas at the same speed. It can perform repetitive tasks with the same accuracy. It is capable to store huge amounts of data and retrieve it whenever required. Limitations The following are the limitations of computer: The computer is a dull machine. It cannot think and give the right decisions as a It cannot operate without electricity or a battery. It cannot produce accurate output if the inputs are inaccurate or wrong. It cannot learn, think, reason, or react like humans.
The following are the advantages and disadvantages of computer:

items: The computer is faster than a human being and any other device ever invented.
The computer can be used for computer crime like hacking, cracking, creating and sending malicious software (Like virus, worm, Trojan horse).
It is an accurate and versatile machine, thus used in different fields like education, hospital, and bank.
It is still expensive device. Repair and maintenance are required frequently.
It can be used for communication among many users like using the Internet.
Skilled manpower is required to work on the computer.
It has a large and permanent storage facility. As a result, data and programs can be stored, modified and used for different purposes

The failure of a device or program can produce unreliable things as a result of the loss of data and information. 📁 Summary at a Glance  The word "computer" comes from the Latin word "computare", which means to calculate.  A computer is a programmable digital automatic machine, which takes input from the user, processes it, and gives the desired output as an information in high speed.  Characteristics or features of Computer are speed, accuracy, automation, diligence, reliability, versatility, and storage capacity.  Capabilities of Computer are; it is capable of performing task automatically, producing 100% accurate output, performing repetitive tasks with same accuracy, storing large amount of data.  Limitations of Computer are; it cannot make decisions as human being, cannot operate without electrical power supply, cannot produce accurate output when the inputs are not accurate.  Advantages of Computer are; it is faster than a human being. It is accurate, reliable and versatile device.  Disadvantages of Computer are; it is used for cyber crimes and spreading malicious computer viruses. Skilled manpower is required to work and increased dependency on the computer.

blocks.text: An abacus consists of a rectangular frame carrying a number of wooden rods. Its mid- bar divides each of these rods into unequal - upper and lower frames. The upper frame is called heaven, whereas the lower frame is called the earth. Heaven consists of two beads, whereas the earth part consists of five beads to each rod. The value of bead on heaven part is five and the earth is one. Calculation is done by moving the beads – up and down in the rod and counting them.

Napier's bones are a manually-operated calculating device created by John Napier. Napier's Bones are numbered rods to help work different multiplication problems. He used bones to demonstrate division by subtraction and multiplication by addition, according to the principle of logarithms. He also published the table of logarithms in 1614 AD. It was very useful in simplifying the multiplication of large numbers. William Oughtred invented a rectangular device-slide-rule in 1620 AD. It was a calculating device, based on the principles of the logarithm. A slide rule consists of two graduated scales, one of which slips upon the other. It can be used to find products and quotient of any Blaise Pascal developed Pascaline. He invented the first numerical mechanical calculating machine (popularly known as Pascaline). This device could perform addition and subtraction up to 8 digits that was a great achievement at that time.

Difference and Analytical Engine Charles Babbage invented the Difference Engine in 1822 AD. Theoretically, it can solve differential equations and calculate various mathematical functions. He continued working on his Difference Engine for a full ten years, but he had a better idea. His new idea was the construction of automatic mechanical counting machine. Babbage called his machine as an Analytical Engine in 1833 AD.

The idea of the Analytical Engine was considered the most significant step in the history of computers, because of his idea only, the dream of modern computers has come true. This Analytical Engine was capable of calculating up to 20 decimals at about 60 additions per minute, could store information, making decisions, and carry out instructions on its decisions. His efforts guided a number of principles, which have been shown to be fundamental to the design of today's digital computers; like, input unit, processing unit, memory and output unit. That's why he was considered the "Father of modern day's computer".

Lady Augusta Ada, (in short lady Ada) was the follower, and assistant of Charles Babbage. She helped revise plans, and communicate the Analytical Engine to the public. Lady Ada's fine understanding of the Analytical Engine allowed her to create the instruction routines and she suggested to Babbage to use Bernoulli numbers. In 1842, Lady Ada documented Babbage's work and wrote programs for Analytical Engine. This plan is now regarded as the first computer program. That's why, she was considered the first computer programmer.

Herman Hollerith developed the Tabulating Machine in 1886 AD. This company was later merged with other companies to form the world-renowned company International Business Machine Hollerith's method used cards to store data which he fed into a machine that compiled the results mechanically. This machine was used for faster computation of population census in the United States. John von Neumann John von Neumann gave the idea of a stored-program computer in the sense that the program is stored internally in the main memory of the computer in 1945. So, he was called the "Father of Stored program". John von Neumann Before that, program required for the computer was integrated and written permanently in chips, so modification of the program was not possible. But after Neumann 'work, such programs were stored inside a computer in some storage media, and, so modification was easy and flexible.

Electromechanical Age The calculator of this age was developed by using a mechanical and electronic component. Some of the developments in this age are: Mark-I It was the first electro-mechanical computer, developed by Howard H. Aiken and the engineers of IBM. The machine was called IBM Automatic Sequence Controlled Calculator (IBM ASCC) and later as Mark-I. It was completed in 1944 AD. It's about 51 feet long, 8 feet height and 3 feet wide i.e.; bulky in size. Technically, it consumed a huge amount of power, and generated a lot of heat during the operation.

In 1939, John Vincent Atanasoff and Clifford Berry designed Atanasoff-Berry Computer (ABC) for solving systems of mathematical simultaneous equations. It is considered as the first computing machine which introduced the idea of binary arithmetic, regenerative memory, and logic circuits.

blocks.text: The features of first generation of computers are enlisted below:

items: Vacuum tube technology is used in the computer.
The operating speed was in terms of millisecond.
Magnetic core memory and magnetic drum were used as the primary devices.
The computers were used for simple mathematical calculation.
Example: ENIAC, EDVAC, EDSAC, UNIVAC.

blocks.text: The second generation of computer began with the development of the transistors. The size of the computers was decreased as vacuum tubes were replaced with transistors. The features of second generation of computers are enlisted below:

items: Transistor was used as the main component.
The operating speed was in terms of microsecond.
Magnetic core memory and magnetic tape were used as the memory devices.
The computers were used for simple and complex scientific calculation.

blocks.text: Example: Leo Mark III, IBM 1620, IBM 7094

The third generation of computer begin with the development of integrated circuits (IC). As scientists managed to fit many components on a single chip, computers became even smaller. The features of third generation of computers are enlisted below:

items: Integrated Circuit (IC) was used as the main technology.
The operating speed of the computer was in terms of nanosecond.
Memory devices like RAM, ROM, floppy disk and hard disk were used.

blocks.text: The computers were used for calculations, record keeping, managing population Example: IBM 360 series, ICL 900 series, Honeywell 200 series.

The fourth generation of computer begin with the development of microprocessor. It started around 1971 AD. The computer used at present are the fourth-generation computers. These computers have faster processing speed and increased memory capacity. The features of fourth generation of computers are enlisted below:

items: Microprocessor or VLSI is used as the main component.
The operating speed of the computer is in terms of picosecond range.

blocks.text: RAM, ROM, cache memory, hard disk, optical memory [CD, DVD, Blue-ray disk (BD)] and flash memory are used as the memory devices. The computers are used for record keeping, scientific calculation, entertainment and communication, engineering, controlling, and health sector. Example: IBM desktop PC, Dell notebook, Hewlett-Packard (HP) laptop, iPad.

Scientists are working on the development of fifth generation computers. It will be based on artificial intelligence. It is believed that the fifth generation of computers will be with genuine IQ. The computers will be able to reason logically and can respond to its surroundings with the use of different types of sensors. The features of fifth generation of computers will be enlisted below: It is based on parallel processing.

Superconductor technology and biochip will be used as the main element of the computer. The operating speed will be in terms of femtosecond. The computers will be used in area, which will require high level of intelligence and The computers will have AI (Artificial Intelligence) software. Some Terms related to the Generations of Computers Some terms related to the generations of computers are: Vacuum tube: A vacuum tube is also known as electron tube, or valve.

It is a device that controls the flow of electrons in a vacuum. It used as the main components in the first generation of computers. Transistor: A transistor is a semiconductor device used to switch electronic signals. It is composed of semiconductor material. It replaced vacuum tube in second generation of computers. It is smaller, reliable, fast, and has low power requirement than vacuum tube. IC:
IC (Integrated circuit) is a small silicon chip that contains large number of electronic components like transistor within it. IC is the major component used in third generation of computers. AI:

AI (Artificial Intelligence) is an ability of artificial object through which it will have ability to learn, think, reason, make decision or react as humans. 📁 Summary at a Glance  Generation of the computer is the division of electronic computers on the basis of technology used by the computer.

Its division based on processing components and memory devices used in the computer.  Classification of generation of computer is mainly based on the basic technology, architecture, and mode of operation. It has been identified that there are four major stages in the continuous development process of computers. These stages are called computer generations.  The first generation computer was the large mainframes built with valves.

The smaller and more reliable computers built with transistors are called second generation computers. The computers made with silicon chips (IC) are the third generation computers. A real break- through came when the microprocessor chip appeared. The microprocessor based computers are called fourth generation computers.  Vacuum tube is also called as electron tube, or just a tube, or valve.

It is a device that controls electric current between electrodes in an evacuated container. It is the main technology used in first generation of computers.  A transistor is a semiconductor device used to switch electronic signals. It is composed of semiconductor material. It replaced vacuum tube in second generation of computers.

Transistor is smaller, reliable, fast switching, and it has low power requirement than vacuum tube.  IC (Integrated circuit) is a small silicon chip that contains large number of electronic components like transistor within it. It is the major technology used in third generation of computers.  AI (Artificial Intelligence) is an ability of artificial object through which it will have ability to learn, think, reason, make decision or react as humans.

blocks.text: Different types of computer on the basis of size are:

Super computer is the fastest computer in terms of processing speed. It is the most expensive among all types of computers. It is usually hybrid and special purpose computer. It is generally used by large corporations, universities, and government agencies, mainly in the areas of defence and weaponry, weather forecasting, scientific research, aeronautics, satellite communication and space administration, and nuclear research work.

Mainframe computer is one of the largest computers on the basis of size. It occupies around 1000 sq. ft area. It contains around 100 Input/output terminals (users). blocks.text: Most keyboards have the following keys. Alphanumeric keys (letters and numbers). Punctuation Keys (comma, semicolon, and so on). Special Keys (function keys, control keys, arrow keys, caps lock keys, and so on).
Mouse

Mouse is a small hand-held pointing and clicking input device used to control the position of the cursor on the screen. It is a small plastic box with two or three buttons on the top. Two rotating wheels inside the mouse detect the movement and the direction of the movement. By pressing the mouse button, the user communicates his/her choice to the computer. The mechanical mouse consists of a ball on its underneath, that translates the mouse movement into digital signals. This mouse contains 1-3 buttons.
Scanner

The scanner is an input device, which is used to enter text, images, and graphs printed on paper directly into the computer. It provides faster and more accurate data entry. It digitizes an image by dividing it into a small grid of boxes and representing each box with either zero or one, whether the box is filled or not.

items: Touchpad It is one of the latest pointing devices. It looks like a small grey window, about two inches wide. The user slides his fingertip across the window to move the cursor on the screen. When the window is tapped, it works as the clicking of a mouse button. It is used in the latest laptops.

blocks.text: Joystick

A joystick is a pointing device that consists of a vertical handle like a gearshift lever mounted on a base with one or two buttons. It is used mainly for playing video games and in some computer-aided design systems. As the handle is moved around, the movement is translated into binary signals with the help of electronic contacts in its base.
Touch Screen
A touch screen is a video display screen that has been sensitized to receive input from the touch of a finger or some pointed object. It is a screen with touch-sensitive points or program icons.

A microprocessor is also known as the Central Processing Unit (CPU). It is the brain of the computer. The first Microprocessor called Intel 4004 was developed by American Intel Corporation in 1971. Components of Microprocessor The microprocessor consists of mainly three components:

items: Arithmetic and Logic Unit (ALU): The ALU performs mathematical computations, and logic operations and controls the speed of those operations as directed by CU. Typically, an ALU performs the following calculations: Addition, subtraction, multiplication, division. Logical AND, logical OR, logical EXCLUSIVE OR, logical NOT (complement).

Control Unit (CU): The control unit of the CPU regulates the flow of data within the processor as the whole operations of the computer system. Hence, the CU acts as the nerve system of the computer system. Functions of the Control Unit: The control unit controls and coordinates the sequence of data movements around the computer system. It receives instructions from RAM and interprets them and sends a relevant control signal to all other devices. It issues control signals that control hardware components within the CPU.

Register: The microprocessor has temporary data holding places called a register. Registers are small amounts of high-speed memory contained within the CPU. The main function of the register is to transfer data for immediate use by the CPU for data processing.

blocks.text: Memory unit or memory storage (In short; memory) is the main component of a computer system that enables it to function and it is used to store data/instructions and programs temporarily (in RAM) and permanently (in a storage device). The digital computer contains two types of memory storage. Types of Memory
Primary Memory

The primary memory stores programs along with data temporarily (inside RAM), and stores necessary programs for the operation of the computer (ROM). Primary memory is located between RAM and CPU. RAM, ROM and Cache Memory are the primary memories. The features of primary memory are: It is directly accessible to the Central Processing Unit. It is used for loading data and programs while they are being used on a computer.
Secondary Memory

Secondary storage is also called auxiliary memory or external or backup memory. It is a non-volatile memory that retains programs even if the power supply is cut off. It is cheaper than primary memory. Secondary memory or storage stores operating systems, data, and application programs permanently. Hard disks, tape drives, CDs, DVDs, and solid-state drives are secondary storage devices. Features of Secondary Memory It has high storage capacity and is used to store data and programs for future use. It is usually slower to read/write operations than primary memory (RAM).

The result after processing is called as output. Output devices are used to provide the output to the user. The outputs can be in the forms like: text, image, audio or video. There are two types of outputs:

items: Softcopy refers to data that is shown on a display screen or sound produced by the speaker. This kind of output is untouchable. It is temporary in nature. For example, contents displayed on a monitor or words spoken out by a voice response system (speaker) are soft copy outputs.

Hardcopy refers to printed output printed on paper that can be touched and carried for being shown to others. It is permanent in nature and can be kept in paper files or can be looked at in the locker. For example, outputs produced on paper in the form of text or/and graphics by printers or plotters are hardcopy outputs.

blocks.text: Monitor

A computer monitor is an output unit, which displays information on the screen in pictorial or textual form. The display screen is used to view the result of the processing. It is the most common and popularly used output device for producing soft copy output. Monitors can be classified as:

items: CRT (Cathode Ray Tube) Monitor: It is a large bulky sized monitor. It is rarely used at present. Due to its size, it is not appropriate for portable devices.

LCD (Liquid Crystal Display) Monitor: LCD is one of the common flat-panel monitors. It creates images with a special kind of liquid crystal. LCD is lighter, not bulky but expensive compared to CRT monitors. It consumes low voltage and low power consumption than CRT. It is widely used in laptops, computers, digital cameras, digital clocks, digital watches, and CD players.

LED (Light Emitting Diode) Monitor: The LED monitor contains an array of light- emitting diodes as a video display. These diodes are turned on or off to display the output. Initially, it was used only for simple digital displays like in the calculator and digital watch. At present, it is the popular monitor for television sets, desktop PC, laptops, mobile phones, and tablet PC.

blocks.text: Printer

The printer is a peripheral device used to print text, pictures, illustrations, figures, and images. It is used to produce hardcopy output i.e., in the permanent readable form. There are two types of printers, Impact printers and non-impact printers.

items: An impact printer forms a character or image by striking a mechanism such as a print hammer or wheel against an inked ribbon, leaving an image on paper. Examples: Dot Matrix printers, Daisy-wheel printers, and Line printers.

The Non-impact printer forms characters and images without making direct physical contact between the printing mechanism and paper. It is faster than an impact printer. Examples: Laser printer, ink-jet printer, thermal printer. 📁 Summary at a Glance  Computer hardware is the physical parts of the computer. It includes input, output, processing, and storage or memory devices.  The input unit is used for entering data and program into the computer system for processing. Providing user interface: A user interface is the layer through which user use the computer. OS provides user interface for using the computer. OS provides two types of user interfaces: GUI (Graphical User Interface) and CUI or TUI (Character User Interface/ text user interface).

sections.title: On the basis of mode of user

items: Single user OS: This type of OS supports only a single user at a time. It is also a single program OS. Example: MS-DOS, PC-DOS, most mobile OS.

Multi user OS: It supports multiple users at the same time. It is also a multitasking OS. It uses time sharing concept to support multiple users and tasks. It shares resources with all the users. Example: Windows 10/8.1/7, UNIX, Linux.

It supports multimedia and Internet. Example: Windows, Mac OS, Android.

CUI based OS: CUI (Character/Command User Interface) based OS contains only the text with no graphics. It has features like: It is difficult and less attractive for the beginners. It doesn't support pointing device like mouse, joystick, touchpad, touch screen and light pen. User needs to understand and remember the command. It doesn't support multimedia and the CUI is faster than GUI. Example: MS DOS, UNIX, Linux.

blocks.text: Learning Objectives After reading this chapter, you will be able to  know the features and uses of word processing,  use word processing software and its features.

Word processor is application software that helps in the creation of a document. It facilitates the creation of documents through computerized text editing, formatting, storing and printing. It allows the user to type text, make corrections without retyping the entire matter and has the feature to make the text look attractive. Some examples of word processor are: MS Word, Word Perfect, Word Star, Lotus Notes.

Different features of word processor are: It is easier and faster to create a document. It is easier to edit the text using tools like insert, delete, modify the documents, and undo/redo, find/replace. It has tools for formatting the documents like bold, italic, underline, different fonts, font size, its colour, and paragraph formatting. Formatting is done for making the document attractive. It can save the document so that it can be opened the next time. It has tools to insert text, objects (picture, graph, etc.) anywhere in the document whenever necessary.
A word processor can be used for designing/creating the following task:

blocks.text: Cell

The intersection between row and column is called a cell in which data can be stored. Cells are surrounded by light-gray line known as gridlines. A cell can be identified its cell address, which is made up of a column heading and row number. The address of first cell is A1. Only one can be active at time and is shown by thick black border, which is called active cell. A cell can contain 32000 characters.

A cell's location in the spreadsheet is referred to as its cell reference. To find a cell reference, simply look at the column headings to find which column the cell is in, and across to find which row it is in. The cell reference is a combination of the column letter and row number - such as A1, B3, or Z345. Specially, cell reference is very important while writing formula or addressing the cell to evaluate the values. For example, we want to add values which are at D2 and D3 so, instead of writing this formula in cell E2, = 34 + 23, write this instead, = D2+D3.
It is an area or collection of number which defines cells into a worksheet e.g. A1:E15.

When you select a cell by clicking it with the mouse, or moving to it using the keyboard, it becomes the active cell. The name Box, on the left of the formula bar displays the reference of the active cell.

MS Excel is a commercial spreadsheet application program written and distributed by Microsoft Inc. This application file name is EXCEL.EXE and its extension is *.XLSX (Microsoft Office 2016) and the older extension.XLS was used up to MS-Excel 2003. Note: As application developed by Microsoft Inc. (MS Excel) is more popular, we are discussing features of application program by using MS Excel 2016. How to Open MS Excel 2016? Click on Start Button (view as Window's Icon). Choose Microsoft-Excel 2016. Press Window's Icon + R on the keyboard. Then a Run dialogue box will display. Type the text Excel (not case sensitive) into Run Click on OK. Then your required program Book1- Microsoft Excel will open. Then MS Excel 2016 screen appears on the screen. Click on the Blank Workbook to create a new Workbook. Now, a blank workbook opens and you can use as per your requirement. Formatting the Data in the Worksheet MS Excel allows to format the data by changing the font type, size and colour. We can fill a cell by using colour. Change the Font Type, Font Size and Font Colour in a Worksheet

items: Select the cell, range of cells, text, or characters that you want to format.

To change the font colour, click on the dropdown arrow of Font Color and select the appropriate colour. Auto Fill Data in the Cells For fast data entry, you can have MS Excel automatically repeat data or you can fill data automatically. Fill in a Series of Numbers, Dates, or Other Built-in Series Items Using the fill handle (fill handle: The small black square in the lower-right corner of the selection. When you point to the fill handle, the pointer changes to a black cross.), you can quickly fill cells in a range with a series of numbers or dates or with a built-in series for days, weekdays, months, or years.

The formula must begin with an equals to sign (=).
After inserting formula, press Enter key to confirm it.

The formula can include: numeric value, cell address, references, constants, operators and functions. Functions in MS Excel Functions in MS Excel MS Excel contains built in/readymade formula. The functions are categorized according to the work they do. Some commonly used functions are discussed below: Adds all the numbers in a range of cells. Syntax: SUM(number1,number2,...) Returns the smallest number in a set of values. Syntax: MIN(number1,number2,...) Returns the average (arithmetic mean) of the arguments. Syntax: AVERAGE(number1, number2,...) Number1, number2,... are 1 to 255 numeric arguments for which you want the average. Returns the serial number of the current date. The serial number is the date-time code used by Microsoft Excel for date and time calculations. If the cell format was General before the function was entered, the result is formatted as a date. Syntax: TODAY( ) Returns the serial number of the current date and time. If the cell format was General before the function was entered, the result is formatted as a date. Syntax: NOW( ) Returns the sequential serial number that represents a particular date. If the cell format was General before the function was entered, the result is formatted as a date. Syntax: DATE(year,month,day) Counts the number of cells that contain numbers and counts numbers within the list of arguments. Use COUNT to get the number of entries in a number field that is in a range or array of numbers. Syntax: COUNT(value1,value2,...) Returns a positive square root. blocks.text: Web Browser

Browser (Web browser) is a software that allows a user to display and interact with webpages. It is the software that is needed to find, retrieve, view and send information over the Internet. HTML (Hyper Text Mark-up Language) is designing language used for designing or creating webpage for Internet. HTML is a set of logical codes called a markup tags, that can be applied and used to define how the text, image or other information is displayed on the browser. Tim Berners Lee designed the original HTML in 1990. Uses of HTML Uses of HTML are: It is used to create and design basic layouts and design It allows embedding text, image, hyperlink, audio and video on the webpage. blocks.text: ICT is growing and being rapidly used at present. We are directly or indirectly dependent on ICT. It has a major impact on humans. With the use of ICT, we can communicate our feelings, thoughts, and information throughout the world. It is being used in almost all areas. Some of the application areas of ICT are:

items: ICT in Education: IT (Information Technology) is studied as a major subject in school and colleges. ICT tools are used as teaching tools in the sector of science, engineering, health, medicine, and almost all areas. It is used as a learning tool in practical classes in schools, colleges, and universities. Education practice like online study and distance learning requires ICT.

ICT in Banking: Computers are used in keeping information on customers' transactions, debit/credit, and creating a balance sheet. Nowadays electronic transaction is possible in banks through ICT such as ATM cards, debit cards, and credit cards are used. Manual records are replaced by banking software.

ICT in Business: E-commerce is emerging with the use of ICT. Online banking and virtual shopping malls have emerged. Online bookstores and online gift centres are facilitating consumers. ICT has helped to make the business globally.

ICT in Health Sector: Computer-controlled devices like CT-SCAN, ultrasound machines, and MRI scan machines are used in the health sector. ICT is also used for keeping records of patients. It is also used for research and development. An Expert system like MYCIN is used in hospitals for effective treatment.

ICT in Communication and Entertainment: ICT is used in communication fields such as the Internet, E-mail, televisions, radio, FM stations, and telecommunication. It is also used for collecting news and information. Communication sectors use ICT tools like telex, emails, video conferences, video phones, and e-fax. In the field of entertainment, it is used in video editing, special effects, animations, and cartoon character movies. 📁 Summary at a Glance  ICT (Information and Communication Technology) is a broad field combining computer science, communication technology, and data storage and information extraction from data.  Positive Impact of ICT in the Society are: it is easier, faster and cheaper communication, it is being used for online and practical based education and entertainment sectors.  It has few negative Impacts of ICT in the society like piracy of software, data theft, and hacking.  Applications of ICT are in: Education, Health Sector, Banking, Communication, Business, and Entertainment.

blocks.text: On the basis of geographical area coverage or geographical spread, network it can be classified into three basic types. They are: Types of Computer Network Local Area Network

The connection of computers within the school building or even within the computer lab is an example of LAN.

items: LAN is easier and cheaper to establish and it has a higher data transmission speed than MAN.

blocks.text: Metropolitan Area Network (MAN) Metropolitan Area Network (MAN) is a large computer network in the large geographical area that include several buildings or even the entire city (metropolis). It is normally composed of a number of smaller LANs. It can use either wired or wireless transmission media. A cable TV network is an example of MAN. The geographical area of the MAN is larger than LAN, but smaller than WAN. MAN has a much wider geographical area coverage for accessing files and it connects a high number of computers than LAN. MAN is expensive to set up, and complex to establish and manage as compared to It provides faster transmission speed and high security and cost-effective services It is difficult to make the system secure.

Wide Area Network (WAN) A Wide Area Network (WAN) is used to interconnect network computers spread over a wide geographical area, including cities, states, countries, and continents. It uses devices like connector, hub, bridge, switch, router, gateway and repeater. These devices are much more expensive than used in LAN and MAN. Internet is a common example of WAN. It is spread to the largest geographical area therefore network services can be provided to the large area. It uses comparatively expensive devices and data transmission speed is usually slower compared to LAN and MAN. Data can be transmitted to any place in the world in a very short time, as a result, most business organizations can spread their business worldwide using WAN. blocks.text: Learning Objectives After reading this chapter, you will be able to  define the concept of computer graphics and know its applications,  know different graphics file formats,  familiarize yourself with Adobe Photoshop.

The general term "Graphics" comes from the Latin word "graphicus", which means "painting or drawing,". We all are familiar with the famous proverb – "A picture is worth a thousand words", convey information more effectively and efficiently than words". Today, computer graphics is a core technology in digital photography, film, video games, cell phone, computer displays, and many specialized applications.

sections.title: Uses or Purposes of Computer Graphics

blocks.text: Uses or purposes of Computer Graphics are: It is used in advertising, books, magazines, and newspapers. It is useful to make cartoon movies and computer games.

Computer Graphics has several applications, some of which are listed below: Graphics presentation in Business. To make sharpening blurred photos. It is used for printing technology and textile design. To produce engineering & architecture drawings in the field of Civil Construction plans. Some of popular computer graphics and image editing software packages, which are in our market, are: Digital Image Suite. The best professional web design Graphical software that can use to create templates and design the webpage. Graphical Software for Web Adobe Photoshop is a premium graphic and web design tool. It is used by millions of artists around the world. It works with images and it can create graphics for web design. Whether we are looking to create banners, posters, websites, or logos, this software can do all for us. It can use in MS Windows and Mac OS.

There are many image file types. Each image file types have its own merit and demerit; for image types, a JPG or PNG is best for web graphics. The primary web file formats are gif (pronounced "jiff"), jpeg ("jay-peg"), and png ("ping") files. All three common web graphic formats are so-called bitmap graphics. There are three file formats for graphics used on the web: JPG, GIF, and PNG. Each of these file formats is designed with a specific purpose, so it is important to understand the differences when we use them on our websites. JPEG (Joint Photographic Experts Groups): This is an ideal image format for all types of photographs. PNG (Portable Network Graphics): This format is perfect for screenshots and other types of imagery where there's not a lot of color data. GIF (Graphics Interchange Format): If you want to show off animated graphics on our site, this is the best image format for us.

Graphics Editing is a process of changing and improving graphics images using an image editor. During the process, images can be modified by an artist using a pen, brush, airbrush, and other "painting" tools. There are many popular graphics editing software in our market. One of the most popular graphics software is Adobe Photoshop.
Adobe Photoshop

Adobe Photoshop is a raster graphics editor developed and published by Adobe Inc. for MS Windows and Mac OS. It was originally created in 1988 by Thomas and John Knoll. Adobe Photoshop is the major photo editing and manipulation software on the market. It is widely used for image editing, retouching, creating image compositions, and adding effects. It is used by designers, web developers, graphic artists, photographers, and creative professionals. Some features of Photoshop are as follows: Working with image: size, mode, adjustment, crop, transform, Extract, Distort. Working with guide, grid and ruler. How to start / open Photoshop Open the Run window (press window key + R). Press Enter key or Click on OK. The Photoshop Workspace When we open the Adobe Photoshop program, it will load up, initialize, and display on the screen with the workspace. This workspace consists of several components that we will use to create our works of art. It has mainly four basic components in a workspace that will use while creating or modifying graphics. These components are: The Title Bar The Menu Bar. The Tool Bar. The Drawing Canvas. The figure below shows each of these components similar to how they will appear on our screen or monitor.
Title Bar

The title bar has several functions. First off, it displays the current name of the image as well as information about the color mode and zoom scale. As we can see in the figure above, by default, the name will be "Untitled-1". The title bar provides several control buttons. As with other applications, we can use these buttons to minimize the drawing canvas. We can easily open a new canvas to click on "File", then "New". When you do so, the "New Canvas Dialog" will appear. You can use this dialog to create your own canvas. [Try it out.] Title our canvas MyFirstCanavas, set the height to 300 pixels and the width to 300 pixels, and hit the "OK" button. When we hit the "OK" button, we should see our new canvas popup. Try creating a second one for practice. This time, title the canvas "MySecondCanvas" and set the size to 3 inches by 3 inches. We should now have two canvases open.
Menu Bar

The Photoshop menu bar consists of File, Edit, Image, Layer, Select, View, Windows, and Help tab. It works similarly to the menu bar in any other application. The Photoshop menu follows the standard keyboard shortcut keys. Press, the ALT+F combination will access the "File" menu and the Ctrl+N combination will access the "New" menu choice from the "File" menu item.
Tool Bar

Let's look at the Photoshop Toolbox, it is the drawing canvas. It holds 20 tools that allow you to paint, select, navigate, and edit images. To select a tool, it is simply clicked on the icon with the mouse. When you do so, several things will happen. For one, the selected tool button will "stick" to let us know it is selected. If we look at the figure on the left, we will see that the "Eraser" tool is currently selected. Photoshop will also remind us which tool we have selected by modifying the look of our pointer to reflect which tool we are currently using. Once selected, a tool can be used to mark up the drawing canvas. For most of today, we will focus on each of the tools in the toolbar, so for now, just get used to having the toolbar at your disposal and selecting different tools.
Palettes

Palettes are essential components of the toolset. For one, palettes help us define the nature of our tools. It helps us customize how the tools in the toolbox perform. For example, we might "sharpen" (make the line thin) or "dull" (make the line thick) our pencil tool using the "Brushes Palette". Palettes also help us perform some of the more complex tasks such as layering or manipulating complex color schemes. By default, there are five palettes. These five palettes are shown in the figure below: Though these five palettes control many different aspects of your drawing, they do share several properties. All palettes are made up of a title bar with close and collapse buttons, a set of tabs, and a list of options for each tab. Further, all palettes have a fly-out menu of options.
Drawing Canvas

The drawing canvas is the area in which you will create and/or modify images. By default, Photoshop gives you a drawing canvas to work with, but you can easily open another one by one using the "New" menu choice from the "File" menu item. The Canvas is the workspace around an existing image, within the image window. Layer data may lie outside of the canvas, but it will be clipped to the canvas when the image is flattened. Every drawing canvas has a title bar with window control buttons and a drawing area. Drawing Things on the Canvas Now, we can start painting things. Actually, I am sure you have already begun to play around with tools in the toolbox. Like any good program, Adobe Photoshop uses a carefully constructed metaphor to transform a very complex computer-aided task into a fun and easy-to-understand process. So why not take advantage of the metaphor? Now imagine a blank canvas, a table full of differently shaped brushes, and various bottles of colored paint.
Choosing Color

The most common customization you will perform is to modify the size of the brush. To do so, you use the "Brushes" tab in the "Options" palette and choose a larger or smaller brush by selecting from the range given. Except for the Pencil tool, brush shapes are always anti-aliased. Thus, you can choose either a hard edge or a soft edge by choosing either the solid or blended edge circles. Choosing a color is easy; you can choose a color by moving your pointer over the desired color in the color chooser square and clicking. Notice in the figure above that we chose light blue. You can see the exact hue highlighted inside the tiny circle in the color chooser square We are almost ready to start making a mess. But first, let us take a look at the set of brushes we have at our disposal. Defining the Brush Photoshop uses the generic term "brush" to represent any of the drawing tools. Thus, the "paintbrush" tool will have a brush and the "pencil" tool will also have a brush. Actually, it helps to think of a brush as the "drawing edge" of whatever drawing tool you are using. Thus, drawing from Photoshop's art studio metaphor, a paintbrush's brush would be the bristles of the paintbrush while a pencil tool's brush would be the pencil's tip. To customize the brush, you should access the "Options" palette. The most common customization you will perform is to modify the size of the brush. To do so, you use the "Brushes" tab in the "Options" palette and choose a larger or smaller brush by selecting from the range given. Except for the Pencil tool, brush shapes are always anti-aliased. Thus, you can choose both a hard edge and a soft edge by choosing either the solid or blended edge circles. Opening an Image File Follow the steps to open a file: Step 1: Click on File Menu > Open … (Press Ctrl+O (Command+O on the Mac) An Open dialog box will appear Step 2: Select the folder of your image file. Step 3: Select the required image file. Step 4: Click on the Open button. Change of Image Size Image size refers to the length and width of a digital image, also called pixel dimensions. Follow the steps to change image size: Step 1: Open the required image file. Step 2: Click on Image Menu > Image Size… (Keyboard shortcut: Alt+i and select image size) An Image Size dialog box will appear. Here, the size of image is 600×886 pixels. Print size is 21.17 cm by 31.26 cm and the resolution is 72 pixels. Step 3: Type the required Width and Height in the pixel dimension section. Note: In the above dialog box, Constrain Proportions is checked. It means if you enter the value of width, the value for height will be proportionately set. Step 4: Change the value of Width and Height in document size section if you want to print it. Note: Think about the resolution of an image. The output will be low quality if you increase the size of low-resolution image. Step 5: Click on the OK button to accept the changes. Note: The smallest addressable element of pixel (Picture Element) resolution refers to the number of pixels in an image. Creating a New Image File Follow the below steps to create new image file: Step 1: Click on File Menu > New... (Shortcut Key: Ctrl + N) A new dialog box will appear. Step 2: Type the required value for width, height and resolution of your page. Step 3: Select Color Mode and Background Contents. Step 4: Click on OK. Now, a blank image file will appear on the workspace.

This palette contains some groups of tools that are used to edit and manipulate images. Here, text tool and some selections tools of tools box are discussed: Note: The character in the bracket in Tools Box is a shortcut key to activate the required tool. For example, press C to activate Crop Tool. Usage of Tool You select a tool by clicking its icon in the toolbox. A small triangle at the lower right of a tool icon indicates hidden tools. Positioning the pointer over a tool displays a tool tip with the tool's name and keyboard shortcut. Using the selecting tools: A. Toolbox B. Active tool C. Hidden tools D. Tool name E. Tool shortcut F. Hidden tool triangle To show or hide the toolbox Choose Window > Tools. In the menu, a check mark indicates that the item is showing. To move the toolbox Drag the toolbox by its title bar. To select a tool Do one of the following: Click the tool's icon. If the icon has a small triangle at its lower right corner, hold down the mouse button to view the hidden tools. Then, click the tool you want to Press the tool's keyboard shortcut. The keyboard shortcut is displayed in its tool tip. To cycle through hidden tools, hold down Shift and press the tool's shortcut key. To enable or disable cycling through a set of hidden tools (Photoshop) Do one of the following: In Windows, choose Edit > Preferences > General. In Mac OS, choose Photoshop > Preferences > General. Select or deselect Use Shift Key for Tool Switch. To display or hide tool tips Do one of the following: In Windows, choose Edit > Preferences > General. (Photoshop) In Mac OS, choose Photoshop > Preferences > General. (ImageReady) In Mac OS, choose ImageReady > Preferences > General. Select or deselect Show Tool Tips.
Type Tool

Type tool is used to add text to your image file. You might have to add text while creating poster, invitation or any other graphical design. You can also apply different effects to text in Photoshop. Adding Text Follow the steps to add text: Step 1: Create a new file or open an existing image file. Step 2: Click on Type tool from Tools panel or simply press "T". Step 3: Choose the desired font, text size and color. Step 4: Click and drag anywhere in the workspace (new image or existing image) window to create a text box. Step 5: A new text layer will be added to your image. Step 6: Type the required text. Moving Text Follow the steps to move text: Select the text layer. Select the Move tool or press V. Click and drag the text to the required location. Edit the Text Follow the steps to edit the text: Double click on the layer icon of the required text or select the type tool and click on the text. The text will be highlighted. Now, you can modify the text, text size and color.
Crop Tool

The Crop tool is an important tool for making adjustments to the overall size of an image. Using the Crop tool affects the size of the whole image, not just a single layer. Generally, it allows us to remove unnecessary outer parts of an image. In Photoshop, we can crop the image using either the crop tool or the selection tool. Follow the below steps to select to crop a part of an image: Step 1: Open a required image file. Step 2: Select the Crop tool from Tools panel or press C to activate crop tool. Step 3: Select the area of the image, which we want to crop the image. Step 4: Click on Image Menu > Crop or Press Enter. blocks.text: The components/elements of multimedia are: Text Graphics or image Components of Multimedia

items: Text: Text includes alphabets, numbers, and symbols. It can be word, a line of a statement or a paragraph. It is the most widely used component for presenting the information. Text is represented on the computer by using ASCII, and UNICODE.

Graphics or image: Graphics or image is the collection of pixels. The image represents picture capture from the real world whereas graphics represent pictures developed by using graphical objects (geometrical shapes). Graphics can express a piece of information in an easier way than the text.

Audio: Audio is the sound, which is audible to human ear. Different types of audio used in multimedia are human voice, instrumental notes, natural sound, etc. It is one of the important components. The video also includes audio.

Video: A video is the continuous frames of static pictures. Generally, when 20-25 frames per second are displayed, it looks like a smooth-running video. Video is the collection of a large number of related images along with the audio. Video contains images, figures, graphs, animation, sound, etc.

Animation: An animation is the sequence of steam images displayed in rapid succession to provide visual effects. It is the displaying of images in a sequence. It provides life to computer-generated images. It is commonly used in cartoons, movies, video games, video, etc.

blocks.text: Application areas of multimedia are:

items: Education: In education, multimedia is used for a computer-based training courses, online classes, CD-ROM-based educational kits, and computer-based simulators for practical classes, and presentations. Study materials containing text, images, audio, and video are more attractive and effective for the teaching/learning process.
Entertainment: Multimedia is commonly used in the entertainment industry mainly for developing special effects in movies, cartoons, games, and interactive animation.

Webpage: Webpage includes multimedia components like text, images, sound, video and to provide information to the user. The use of multimedia components makes a webpage more attractive and informative.
Business: In business, multimedia is used for advertising such as television, and web-based advertisement. It is used for meetings, presentations, and forecasting related to business.
Communication: Popular communication media at present like audio/video chat, video conferencing, Internet use multimedia for sharing information.
Sports: In sports, multimedia is used for scoring, presenting scores, live telecasts, helping to make decisions for umpire/referees, predications, etc.
Weather forecasting: It includes multimedia for presenting climatic conditions to the viewers, presenting the position of clouds, chance of rain, etc.
Engineering: Multimedia is used for designing the product (prototyping) before it is actually developed. Multimedia-based simulators are used for training the users.

Some major elements of QBASIC programming are: Elements of QBASIC Programming Operators, Expression and Operands

QBASIC has a set of characters, which can be used in variables, constants, operators, and labels. A set of characters, which are valid in QBASIC is known as the QBASIC character set. The QBASIC character set consists of alphabets, numbers and special characters (*, &, >, etc.)
Keyword
Keywords are reserved words, which have predefined meaning in QBASIC. E.g.; CLS, REM, INPUT, PRINT, LET, VAL.
Data is any value given to the program. Data are processed to get output in the program. Basically, QBASIC supports two types of data: Numeric: only numbers String: any alphanumeric values
Variable

A variable is an entity that can be changed during the execution of the program. There are two types of variables in QBASIC: numeric and string variables. a. Numeric variable: In QBASIC numeric variables can be an integer, long integer, single-precision, or double-precision.

blocks.text: In QBASIC variable can be declared by using two techniques: a. Implicit declaration: Implicit declaration is the default method of declaring variables in QBASIC. Using this method, we can declare a variable at the time of assigning value to the variable. One should take care of the type declaration symbol during the declaration and use of variables. One can use a LET statement to declare variables implicitly but a LET statement is not mandatory in newer versions of QBASIC. Example: A$= "Computer" b. Explicit declaration: Explicit declaration of a variable is done before the use of variables. The DIM statement is used to declare variables explicitly in QBASIC. E.g.; DIM a AS INTEGER, DIM b AS STRING, etc. It is not mandatory to use a type declaration symbol while declaring variables explicitly. Also, as all variables are declared at the top, programmers are less prone to use the same variable name for different purposes.
